why: Low islands under a steady sea wind and warm rain, paddies and mangrove coasts, sea on every side.
A breezy island in Topal Bay with salt spray and sea mist.
Humid lowland jungle and riverine forest under tall hardwoods; rain and fog the commonest weathers, sea fog on the coast.
A ridge of firm ground above the marsh, breezy and a little drier, morning mist below and wide views.
Hot and humid with steam rising off the water after rain; dark water between islets; 561 of its 902 cells are blackwater swamp.
Fen and sedge with reed beds and frequent rain; 236 pond and 83 green-marsh cells.
The south-eastern sea under a fixed grey overcast and a steady swell, off the Padomaic.
Long rains and fog over the bogs of a flooded hillscape; 267 blackwater and 772 pond cells (bog pools).
Sea mist from the Sea of Mists on the south coast, frequent rain, mangrove edges and salt creeks.
Mesa tops 60 to 110 m above the lowland, drier than the jungle, sharp winds, cold nights after hot days.
Grey mud-flats and sandy points on the Padomaic shore, frequent rain and sea fog; 119 sea cells.
Mangrove delta on Topal Bay: hot, frequent heavy rain, fog off the estuary at dawn.
A wide pale lake fringed with reed and delta marsh, squalls over open water and fog on the shores; 77 green-marsh cells round the lake.
A dark wood of huge roots: light comes green and dim, the air thick; morning fog and heavy rain; braided river arms (204 river cells).
A river plain with low banks, cut by channels, low cloud over the channels; rivers and streams are its water.
A bayou of reed flats under heavy warm rain and low mist; 408 green-marsh cells.
Red mounds in green-grey marsh, pale lakes and brown creeks; 452 green-marsh cells, the most of any region.
The open eastern ocean: overcast and rainy with sea mist, bright on clear days.
Warm and humid with mist most mornings; rain and thunderstorms are common.
A windy rock island off the east coast, salt-laden and drier than the mainland, with sea fog and rain.
A warm bay with sea breezes, sea fog and passing rain storms, facing the sunset.
Hot, humid and still, rain most days, brown water and mist; 331 cells blackwater swamp, the most of any region after Banujha.
A grey-green maze of cattails and black water with a warm fog on the channels; 168 of 301 cells blackwater swamp.
A rolling river plain with heavy rain and thunder; the river and its branches carry the causeways; 85 stream cells.
